name: Wyoming

law.summary: No Wyoming statute, rule or guidance found that requires public notice of a sewage overflow. Collection-system owners report SSOs to WDEQ verbally within 24 hours and in writing within five days; WDEQ's spill and complaint database is staff-only.

citations.cite: WDEQ WYPDES Sanitary Sewer Overflows guidance
citations.title: SSO reporting
citations.quote: Reporting of the SSO should occur verbally within 24 hours of becoming aware of the event.
citations.who: owners or operators of wastewater collection systems and treatment works
citations.deadline: 24 hours verbal; written within five days

regulator_report.cite: WDEQ SSO guidance; WYPDES permit standard conditions (not read)

bills_and_cases: Water Quality Rules Chapter 4 revised (filed 2026-01-12); oil and hazardous substances only (search only).

statewide_feed.notes: No public list of reported overflows or spills that include sewage found.

sso.notes: SSO reports go to the state agency only.

habs.program: WDEQ/WDH Harmful Cyanobacterial Bloom advisories (bloom and toxin)
habs.notes: Historical layer machine-readable to 2025; current year in Story Map and email bulletins.

barriers.note: Ask WDEQ for a public view.

barriers.what: SSOs reported verbally to WDEQ; no public duty
Current-year HCB advisories published as GovDelivery bulletins and Story Map text, not a live layer

readiness.rationale: No overflow feed, no SOBE rows, no CSOs, no public duty; the spill database is login-only. HCB advisories are the only live water-risk source.

owner_questions: Subscribe to WDEQ HCB GovDelivery bulletins?
Ask WDEQ to open a public view of deqspills incidents (SSOs included?).
surprise: Wyoming built a modern spills app with incident search, but every search route is behind a staff login; the public can only file reports, not read them.
